newsitem.title: USA: Tyson says tackling Medicare problem a priority.
newsitem.headline: Tyson says tackling Medicare problem a priority.

text.p: Carrying out a plan to prevent insolvency in the Medicare trust fund will be a priority for President Clinton if he is re-elected, a top White House economic adviser said Tuesday.

"I think as one of the first actions of the second term of the president and a new Congress, we should in fact work together to deal with the medium-term issue," Laura Tyson, chairwoman of Clinton's National Economic Council, told a breakfast organized by Reuters.
The medium-term issue she was referring to was the projected insolvency in the early part of the next century of the Medicare "Part A" trust fund.
"We understand the parameters of that problem and it can be addressed without any significant adjustments in the structure of the program," Tyson said.

The Clinton administration official, however, said she felt it was important to draw a distincton between the medium-term issues relating to Medicare and the longer-term issues. She also stressed the importance of differentiating between the situations with Medicare and Social Security.
"The longer-term problems are the demographics problems," Tyson said, adding that there is plenty of time to make changes to resolve those problems appropriately.
Concerning the Social Security situation, Tyson said she is disheartened when people often refer to that as a "crisis."

"There is no crisis in the Social Security system," she said. "The Social Security system has a 75-year horizon during which a financing deficit arises. The financing is not large relative to the size of the economy."
